summary: POC scoping call to decide between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment for Acme Health's clinical summarization workload. Customer cares about latency (P95), throughput predictability, and PHI handling / compliance. Agreed to run a 2-week benchmark comparing Hosted (burst to dedicated) vs Dedicated (reserved GPUs) and to evaluate a Private (VPC/on-prem) timeline for later phase. Next steps: pricing, benchmark plan, sample prompts.
topics: Workload sizing (RPS, tokens per request, concurrency)
Deployment tradeoffs: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-15
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE); Maya Patel (Redwood SE); Sara Lopez (CTO, Acme Health); Devon Price (Head of ML); Avery Kim (Infra Lead)

Summary: Short scoping session to align on POC goals, sizing, and the tradeoffs between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes. We cover benchmarks to run, success criteria, and an initial timeline. Transcript quality: medium (some auto-transcription errors).

[00:00] Liam (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time. quick intro — i'm liam, i'm the AE on the account, maya is our systems engineer, sara/devon/avery — thanks for joining. are we all good to go for a 45-60 minute scoping?
[00:18] Sara (Acme CTO): yep good to go. main thing for us is PHI handling and making sure any POC won't accidentally egress patient info, so security and data residency are hard requirements.
[00:30] Devon (Acme Head of ML): and from ML side we need stable latency — P95 ideally <250ms for short clinical summarization calls — but we'll tolerate up to 500ms during peak if cost benefits are large. also need to measure token cost per 1M requests.
[00:50] Maya (Redwood SE): ok that's helpful. can you walk through current traffic profile? avg requests per minute, token counts, concurrency?
[01:02] Avery (Infra): sure — baseline is ~30 reqs/sec during business hours, spikes to 90 reqs/sec for short windows. avg prompt+response tokens ~1,100 tokens, but 80% are under 800 tokens. concurrency target is 100 simultaneous inference slots.
[01:25] Liam: great, that maps to about ~3M tokens/day rough estimate at baseline, spike days double that. for the POC we typically do a representative slice — say 10-20% traffic but include peak bursts — does that sound reasonable?
[01:40] Sara: yes, and we want to validate correctness too — clinical fidelity matters; hallucination rates must be tracked.
[01:47] Maya: we'll run evaluation prompts and we can hook into your QA set. for benchmarks we'll run three vectors: hosted baseline (our hosted infra), dedicated reserved fleet sized for your peaks, and a private (VPC or on-prem) smoke test focusing on networking and KMS.
[02:05] Devon: curious on what the hosted limits are — can hosted handle 90 rps with P95 <250? what's the SLAs?
[02:13] Liam: hosted can scale but with some variability; for consistent P95 under 250ms at 90 rps we'd likely advise a dedicated pool. Hosted is great for fast ramp and lower ops overhead; dedicated buys predictability and isolation. privately managed (Private) is the strictest — full control for PHI but longer lead time.
[02:30] Maya: tech note — for long context workloads we use KV cache and continuous batching; that reduces cost and improves tail latency. for dedicated we can tune kernel selection and quantization to meet latency/cost targets.
[02:48] Avery: about encryption — can you integrate with our KMS? we need HSM-backed keys for production but for POC standard KMS is sufficient?
[02:57] Liam: yes we support customer-managed keys (KMS) and HSM for Private deployments. for hosted we can do Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) with a managed integration; dedicated gives stronger isolation.
[03:12] Devon: timeline question — how long to stand up dedicated for a pilot vs hosted?
[03:18] Maya: hosted is immediate; dedicated typically 2-3 weeks for reserved capacity provisioning and validation; private (VPC) depends on network approvals — plan 4-8 weeks if no blockers, on-prem air-gapped could be longer.
[03:33] Sara: ok so operability and procurement timelines matter. we need security package for the board review next monday.
[03:40] Liam: we'll send SOC2 + ISO docs and our network diagram.
[03:44] Maya: and i'll attach the dedicated sizing guide so you can see GPU counts and expected token/sec capacity.
[03:50] Devon: on benchmarks — what are the standard tests? we want end-to-end latency (including network), cold-starts, KV cache hit/miss, and throughput scaling.
[03:58] Maya: right — our plan: 1) synthetic load generator to hit RPS targets 2) run production prompt set for quality and output diffs 3) KV cache experiments (cold vs warmed) 4) quantized model runs (8-bit/4-bit) to measure cost vs quality tradeoff. each run 24-48 hours for stability.
[04:18] Liam: and we'll capture token counts, P50/P95/P99 latencies, cost estimate, and qualitative evals from your clinical reviewers.
[04:27] Sara: what about fallbacks — if a model degrades do you have automatic fallback to smaller models or degraded modes?
[04:33] Maya: yes we support routing policies — you can have canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant or to a cached response. that's part of Redwood Console.
[04:44] Devon: can we test KV cache correctness? for clinical data dedup and privacy we need to ensure prefixes don't leak across tenants.
[04:53] Maya: dedicated and private provide tenant isolation for KV caches. hosted has logical isolation too, but for PHI we usually recommend dedicated or private depending on your regs.
[05:05] Avery: on cost — what's the delta we should expect between hosted and dedicated? rough ballpark per 1M tokens?
[05:12] Liam: depends on utilization. hosted per-token is slightly higher but you pay for convenience. dedicated amortizes the GPU cost so at steady-state >60% utilization it becomes cheaper. we'll send a model-specific price table but expect 20-40% savings at medium-heavy utilization.
[05:28] Devon: and private? on-prem might be cheapest on raw compute but ops and procurement make it expensive overall.
[05:34] Liam: exactly — private has hidden costs: networking approvals, infra ops, and longer lead time. also model compatibility — if you want our managed runtime in air-gapped you'll need our on-prem package.
[05:45] Sara: decision criteria for us: 1) Security/compliance (PHI), 2) Latency SLAs, 3) Cost per 1M tokens, 4) Integrations (KMS, SSO), 5) Time-to-production. does that align with what you hear?
[05:59] Maya: yep that's consistent. we'll map the POC to those criteria: Weighted scoring during the POC — e.g., 30% security, 30% latency, 20% cost, 20% accuracy.
[06:10] Liam: practical POC outline: Week 0 (now): Agree sample prompts and traffic slice. Week 1: onboarding and hosted baseline run. Week 2-3: dedicated provisioning + benchmarking. Week 4: private/VPC smoke if needed and evaluation + scoring, then decision meeting. total ~4 weeks for initial decision if no network approvals.
[06:27] Devon: sounds good. for benchmarks please include model version pinning and quantization notes because our QA will need consistent runs.
[06:35] Maya: we'll freeze model hashes and config, and store logs. also will provide reproducible harness script.
[06:42] Avery: network / firewall rules — we'll need IP ranges and egress ports. provide a minimal set for the POC.
[06:48] Liam: will include in the onboarding doc.
[06:52] Sara: any red flags/risks?
[06:55] Maya: potential roadblocks are procurement lead time for Dedicated, internal security review for BYOK/HSM, and data residency approvals for Private. we mitigated these by doing hosted baseline while approvals progress.
[07:10] Liam: ok final recap — deliverables from Redwood: pricing + sizing sheet, SOC2/ISO + network diagram, benchmark plan + harness, and a scheduled window for the end-to-end run week of 4/27. deliverables from Acme: sample prompt set, traffic profile, and firewall approvals where possible.
[07:29] Sara: thanks — we'll aim to have the prompt set by 4/18 and confirm the decision stakeholders.
[07:35] Devon: one more quick Q — for Dedicated, what's the SLA for failover between regions?
[07:41] Maya: dedicated supports multi-region replication but cross-region failover is best-effort in pilot; production SLA options exist for full geo-redundancy. we'll scope that if you need it.
[07:52] Liam: cool — we'll follow up with the docs. thanks everyone.
[07:57] Sara: thanks, bye.
